hints: Focus on what type of bonding is in SiCl4 and which atom pulls electrons more strongly.
Recall that covalent molecular chlorides of Period 3 get less volatile from NaCl down to SiCl4, and SiCl4 is a simple molecular liquid.
Remember that Si can expand its octet to accept water, so think about what hydrolysis of SiCl4 forms and whether HCl and SiO2 fit the description.
walkthrough:
**Check polarity from electronegativity**

Chlorine is much more electronegative than silicon, so each Si-Cl bond is polar covalent with electrons pulled toward Cl.

Bond polarity: $\text{Si}^{\delta+} - \text{Cl}^{\delta-}$

**Check state at room temperature**

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is a simple covalent tetrahedral molecule with only weak van der Waals forces between molecules.

It has a low boiling point (about 58 degrees C), so it is a fuming liquid at room temperature. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check hydrolysis with water**

Unlike $\text{CCl}_4$, Si can use vacant 3d orbitals to accept a lone pair from water, so it hydrolyses vigorously.

Hydrolysis equation:
$$\text{SiCl}_4(l) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2(s) + 4\text{HCl}(aq)$$

**Put the three statements together**

$\text{SiO}_2$ is a white solid precipitate and $\text{HCl}$ gives a strongly acidic solution, so statement 3 is correct.

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, the combination with all three is the answer.

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Statement 1 is true from electronegativity, statement 2 is true as SiCl4 is a molecular liquid, and statement 3 is true from hydrolysis to SiO2 and HCl.
options.B: Incorrect, because this combination leaves out statement 3. SiCl4 does hydrolyse in water to give white SiO2 precipitate and acidic HCl, so statement 3 cannot be omitted.
options.C: Incorrect, because this combination leaves out statement 1. Cl is more electronegative than Si, so Si is definitely delta+ and Cl is delta-, so statement 1 is true and must be included.
options.D: Incorrect, because this includes only statement 1. Statements 2 and 3 are also true, SiCl4 is a liquid at room temperature and it hydrolyses to an acidic solution plus precipitate.
